generate_edge_cases.sh.notes: RAR5 steps run the rarlab-7.20 image, RAR4 steps (-ma4) the rarlab-6.24 image. random_512.bin and random_4k.bin come from /dev/urandom, so their archives can only ever be regenerated from the checked-in originals. Steps [6/12] and [5/9] name rar5/rar5_solid.rar and rar4/rar4_solid.rar, but those paths are Scryer e2e imports and must not be overwritten by this script.

generate_encrypted.sh.notes: -p data-only encryption with the corpus password; every run draws fresh KDF salts and IVs, so regeneration is shape-identical only. Its `rm -f rar5_enc_*.rar` cleanup also matches generate_stored_layout.sh's rar5_enc_mv_store_pair and rar5_enc_store_pair sets.

generate_generated_matrix.sh.notes: The MKV input comes from `rarpar-bench payload video` (the shared pinned encoder); the checked-in originals/generated_matrix_clip.mkv predates that and was written by an unpinned host ffmpeg (Lavf62). RAR steps stamp times into headers; -p sets draw random salts.

generate_heavy_damage.sh.notes: The ~80 MB MKV input comes from `rarpar-bench payload video`; RAR from the rarlab-7.20 image; PAR2 from the par2cmdline-turbo 1.4.0 image. The checked-in set predates those pins: its writer was the unrecorded `e2e-archive-tools:latest` image, its .par2 files say 'Created by par2cmdline version 1.1.1', and the clip came from an unpinned host ffmpeg. bench/rarpar-bench/config/corpus.json imports this set by a pinned digest (par2-heavy-damage-28/-250), so a regeneration is a benchmark-corpus change too.

generate_ppmd_perf.py.notes: Refuses any rar whose banner is not RAR 6.24; deterministic in-script payload with a fixed mtime, so the archive is expected to reproduce byte-for-byte, but that has not been demonstrated and is not claimed. Payload digests are pinned in the fixtures README.

generate_rar5_filter_bounds.py.notes: Pure bit assembly: every container and bitstream byte is emitted by the script; re-run 2026-08-16 reproduced the checked-in bytes exactly. POLICY NOTE: its ORACLE_CRCS member checksums were obtained by running unrar as a decompression oracle on the blank build (see the script comment) — unrar is in the generation loop for those six values.

generate_real_world.sh.notes: The MKV input comes from `rarpar-bench payload video`; RAR from the rarlab-7.20 / rarlab-6.24 images; PAR2 from the par2cmdline-turbo 1.4.0 image. The checked-in sets predate every one of those pins: source/generated_sample_clip.mkv was written by an unpinned host ffmpeg (Lavf62), the archives by the rar:latest / rar:4 images, and the .par2 files carry 'Created by par2cmdline version 1.1.1'.

generate_stored_layout.sh.notes: RARLAB rar 7.20 explicitly (the script says so); inputs are fixed-seed python blobs written inline. Header shapes are stable, bytes are not (times, salts).

generate_vm_output_bounds.py.notes: Pure bit assembly with a fixed DOS timestamp; re-run 2026-08-16 reproduced the checked-in bytes exactly. POLICY NOTE: as with generate_rar5_filter_bounds.py, the ORACLE_CRCS member checksums were learned from unrar used as a decompression oracle on the blank build.

weaver.notes: The crates were ported from weaver (rarpar 6b591bc, 2026-07-05); this is the last weaver commit carrying the fixture corpus, under engines/weaver-unrar/ and engines/weaver-par2/, and it is reachable from main and every weaver-v0.7.x/0.8.x tag. Regenerating any of them on the pinned toolchain is a deliberate corpus revision.
